name: Souvlaki
description: Small pieces of meat, in Greece usually pork, grilled on a skewer and often eaten straight off it. It is also served in a rolled pita with tomato, onion, tzatziki and fried potatoes; around Athens the skewers are called kalamaki.
how_to_eat: Eat the pita wrap by hand, or the skewers off the plate with chips.
how_to_order: Ask for 'souvlaki pita' at a souvlatzidiko (souvlaki shop).

name: Gyros
description: Meat cooked on a vertical rotisserie and sliced, served in pita with tomato, onion, fried potatoes and tzatziki. In Greece it is traditionally pork, sometimes chicken, and it is a common street food.
how_to_eat: Eat wrapped in pita, by hand.
how_to_order: Order 'gyro pita' with 'pita me ola' for all the toppings.

name: Moussaka
description: Baked layers of aubergine (sometimes potato), spiced minced meat in tomato sauce and a thick béchamel topping. The Greek version was popularised in the 1920s by chef Nikolaos Tselementes.
how_to_order: Ask for 'moussaka' at tavernas, usually as a ready-cooked 'mageirefta' dish.

name: Pastitsio
description: Baked dish of tubular pasta, a middle layer of minced meat in tomato sauce spiced with cinnamon and cloves, and a béchamel topping. The modern version was created by chef Nikolaos Tselementes and is often served as a main course with a salad.
how_to_order: Order by the portion at tavernas.

name: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
description: 'Village salad' of tomatoes, cucumber, onion and olives topped with a slice of feta, dressed with olive oil, salt and oregano. Green pepper and capers are common additions, and it is served without lettuce.
how_to_eat: Mop up the oil and tomato juice with bread.
how_to_order: Ask for a 'horiatiki' at any taverna.

name: Tzatziki
description: Dip of strained yogurt, grated cucumber, garlic and olive oil. Served as a meze and as the sauce for souvlaki and gyros.
how_to_eat: Eat with bread or as a sauce on grilled meat.
how_to_order: Order as a meze at tavernas.

name: Loukoumades
description: Small deep-fried balls of yeast dough soaked in honey or syrup and topped with cinnamon, walnuts or chocolate sauce. A popular street food, especially in southern Greece, with roots in the ancient Greek enkrides.
how_to_eat: Eat hot, straight from the fryer.
how_to_order: Buy a portion at a loukoumades shop.

name: Frappé
description: Foamy iced coffee made by shaking instant coffee with water and ice, with sugar and milk optional. Invented in Thessaloniki in 1957, it is among the most popular forms of coffee in Greece.
how_to_eat: Sip slowly through a straw; Greeks make one last for hours.
how_to_order: Say how sweet: 'sketo' (no sugar), 'metrio' (medium) or 'glyko' (sweet), and 'me gala' for milk.

name: Spanakopita
description: Savoury pie of phyllo pastry filled with chopped spinach, feta, onions or scallions, egg and herbs such as dill. A fasting version without cheese or eggs is eaten during Lent.
how_to_eat: Eat warm or at room temperature, by the slice.
how_to_order: Buy a slice at a bakery (fournos) or order at tavernas.

name: Fasolada
description: Soup of dried white beans cooked with onion sautéed in olive oil, tomato, and often celery and carrot. It is sometimes called the 'national food of the Greeks'.
how_to_eat: Eat with bread, olives and feta on the side.
how_to_order: Look for it as a daily dish in tavernas, especially in winter.

name: Gigantes Plaki
description: Large white 'giant' beans baked in a tomato sauce with onion, carrot, parsley and olive oil. Served as a meze or a main course, and suitable for Orthodox fast days.
how_to_order: Order as a meze or main at tavernas.

name: Stifado
description: Stew of meat, such as beef, rabbit, hare or pork, cooked with lots of baby onions, tomatoes, wine or vinegar, olive oil and bay leaf. Its name comes from the Italian stufato.
how_to_order: Ask for 'moschari stifado' (beef) or 'kouneli stifado' (rabbit).

name: Kleftiko
description: Lamb slow-cooked with garlic, lemon and herbs, traditionally sealed in a pit or wrapped in paper, until it falls off the bone. Named after the klephts, mountain rebels who hid their cooking.
how_to_order: Ask for 'arni kleftiko' at tavernas.

name: Galaktoboureko
description: Semolina custard baked between layers of buttered phyllo, then covered in syrup. Popular across Greece, with notable versions in Athens and Thessaloniki.
how_to_order: Buy a piece at a zacharoplasteio (pastry shop).

name: Baklava
description: Layers of thin phyllo filled with chopped nuts, baked and soaked in a syrup of sugar, honey and citrus, flavoured with cinnamon. In Greece it is made mostly with walnuts in the north and almonds in the south.
how_to_order: Buy by the piece at pastry shops.

name: Diples
description: Thin sheets of dough folded into bows or spirals, deep-fried and dipped in honey or sugar syrup, then sprinkled with walnuts and cinnamon. A dessert from the Peloponnese, served at weddings and New Year.
how_to_order: Look for them in pastry shops in the Peloponnese.

name: Bougatsa
description: Phyllo pastry filled with semolina custard (or cheese or minced meat), served dusted with sugar and cinnamon. Its modern version comes from Serres and Thessaloniki, where it is sold in special bougatsa shops as a breakfast.
how_to_eat: Eat warm for breakfast with coffee.
how_to_order: Order 'bougatsa me krema' (custard) at a bougatsa shop in Thessaloniki.

name: Koulouri Thessalonikis
description: Ring-shaped bread covered in sesame seeds, a type of simit. Koulouri Thessalonikis is a local product of Macedonia and a common part of a Greek breakfast.
how_to_eat: Eat on the go as breakfast.
how_to_order: Buy one from a street vendor or bakery.

name: Trigona Panoramatos
description: Triangles of buttered phyllo, baked, briefly dipped in syrup and filled with a cream made with milk and egg yolks. A Thessaloniki sweet, also called Thessaloniki triangles.
how_to_order: Buy at pastry shops in Thessaloniki.

name: Soutzoukakia Smyrneika
description: Oblong meatballs of minced meat, breadcrumbs and egg, spiced with cumin, cinnamon and garlic, floured, fried and simmered in tomato sauce. Brought to Greece by Greek refugees from Asia Minor.
how_to_eat: Eat with rice or chips.
how_to_order: Order at tavernas and mageiria (cook-shops).

name: Tsipouro
description: Strong un-aged brandy distilled from grape pomace, plain or flavoured with anise. Made especially in Thessaly, Epirus and Macedonia, it has had EU protected status since 2006.
how_to_eat: Drink in small glasses with a plate of meze; many add water or ice.
how_to_order: Order a 'karafaki' (small carafe) at a tsipouradiko, which brings free meze with each round.

name: Dakos
description: Soaked barley rusk (paximadi) topped with chopped tomato, crumbled feta or mizithra, olive oil and oregano, often with olives and capers. A Cretan salad and meze.
how_to_eat: Let the rusk soften in the tomato juice before eating.
how_to_order: Order as a meze at Cretan tavernas.

name: Kalitsounia
description: Small Cretan pies filled with mizithra cheese mixed with egg and herbs, or with herbs alone, baked or fried. Sweet versions are topped with honey or flavoured with cinnamon.
how_to_order: Buy at bakeries in Crete or order at tavernas.

name: Staka me Avga
description: Eggs cooked in staka, a Cretan dairy product made from the soured cream of sheep's or goat's milk heated with a little flour. A traditional Cretan dish.
how_to_eat: Scoop it up with bread.
how_to_order: Ask for 'staka me avga' at village tavernas.

name: Antikristo
description: A traditional Cretan way of cooking meat, especially lamb, also called ofto. It is one of the island's meat specialities.
how_to_order: Order at Cretan tavernas, often in the mountain villages.

name: Sfakiani Pita
description: Thin pan-fried pie from Sfakia in Crete, filled with mizithra cheese and drizzled with honey, sometimes with sesame seeds. Eaten as a snack or dessert.
how_to_eat: Eat hot with honey.
how_to_order: Order at tavernas in Sfakia and around Chania.

name: Gamopilafo
description: 'Wedding pilaf': rice cooked in broth from goat and rooster. A Cretan speciality.
how_to_order: Look for it at Cretan tavernas, especially in the mountain villages.

name: Tsikoudia (Raki)
description: Clear pomace brandy distilled once from grape residue, without flavourings. In eastern Crete it is called raki, and it is often served chilled as a free digestif in Cretan restaurants.
how_to_eat: Sip in small glasses, often offered free after a meal.
how_to_order: Ask for 'raki'; tavernas often bring it free with dessert.

name: Pastitsada
description: Veal, beef or poultry braised in a spiced tomato sauce with wine, cinnamon and cloves, served over pasta with grated cheese. A traditional Sunday dinner on Corfu, showing Italian influence.
how_to_order: Order at tavernas in Corfu.

name: Sofrito
description: Slices of beef, floured and fried, then slowly cooked with vinegar, garlic and parsley, often with white wine, into a thick white sauce. One of Corfu's best-known dishes.
how_to_eat: Eat with mashed potatoes or rice.
how_to_order: Order at Corfiot tavernas.

name: Bourdeto
description: Fish cooked with onion and a sauce of sweet and hot red pepper, traditionally made with scorpionfish. A Corfiot speciality whose name comes from the Venetian brodetto.
how_to_order: Order at fish tavernas in Corfu.

name: Kumquat Liqueur
description: Sweet liqueur made from kumquats, which in Greece are grown mainly on Corfu and the other Ionian Islands. A typical drink of Corfu.
how_to_eat: Sip chilled after a meal.
how_to_order: Buy bottles in shops across Corfu.

name: Sykomaida
description: Cake of sun-dried figs kneaded with grape must, ouzo and spices such as fennel seed and black pepper; some recipes add almonds or walnuts. A traditional Corfiot sweet, first made to preserve figs for winter.
how_to_eat: Eat in thin slices, e.g. with cheese or a drink.
how_to_order: Buy at Corfiot food shops.

name: Santorini Fava
description: Creamy purée of split peas, served as a dip or main dish. The 'Fava Santorinis' version, made from Spanish vetchling (Lathyrus clymenum) grown only on Santorini and nearby islands, has EU Protected Designation of Origin status.
how_to_eat: Eat warm or at room temperature with bread.
how_to_order: Order as a meze at tavernas on Santorini.

name: Tomatokeftedes
description: Fritters of crushed tomatoes kneaded with flour, onion, mint, parsley and spices, fried in oil. An appetizer of Santorini and the Cyclades, made with Santorini-grown tomatoes.
how_to_order: Order as a meze at tavernas in the Cyclades.

name: Revithada
description: Chickpeas with onions, olive oil and bay leaves, baked overnight in a ceramic pot in a wood-fired oven. A Sunday lunch tradition on Sifnos.
how_to_order: Look for it at tavernas on Sifnos, often on Sundays.

name: Melekouni
description: Soft bar of unhulled sesame, almonds and honey, flavoured with orange peel and spices, offered at engagements, weddings and baptisms on Rhodes. 'Melekouni' is an EU Protected Geographical Indication.
how_to_order: Buy wrapped bars in shops and bakeries on Rhodes.

name: Ouzo
description: Clear anise-flavoured spirit that turns milky white when mixed with water. It is an EU protected geographical indication for Greece and Cyprus; Plomari on Lesbos is considered the home of ouzo.
how_to_eat: Add water or ice and drink slowly with meze.
how_to_order: Order a small bottle ('karafaki') at an ouzeri, which serves meze with it.
